newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik warlord ignores order to withdraw from town.
newsitem.headline: Tajik warlord ignores order to withdraw from town.

text.p: The commander of the Tajik government's elite armoured brigade ignored a command from his president to return to barracks after his forces clashed with an independent armed band on Wednesday.

Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev, who led an armed revolt against the government last year, sent in troops and armour on Wednesday near the aluminium producing town of Tursunzade, about 45 km (30 miles) west of the capital Dushanbe.
Khudoyberdyev said he had moved his troops toward Tursunzade to disarm the band, led by local strongman Kodir Abdulayev, because the group had stolen weapons from his men last month.
"They must hand over their weapons. If they do so, we will allow them to leave," Khudoyberdyev told journalists. "If they refuse, we will take tough measures."

Torn apart by a four-year civil war, Tajikistan's secular government and its armed Islamist opponents have been holding peace talks in the Iranian capital Tehran this week and a ceasefire between the two sides appears to be holding.
But the commander's action bodes ill for chances of peace in a remote, mountainous republic bordering Afghanistan and China, which is riven by regional and clan rivalries.
The unauthorised intervention by Khudoyberdyev, who led an anti-government revolt a year ago, prompted apparent alarm among the beleaguered Tajik leadership in Dushanbe.
Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov ordered the brigade back to its base in the southern town of Kurgan-Tyube, saying it should start pulling out by 4 p.m. (1100 GMT) on Wednesday.
"If he does not obey orders, his actions will be considered a war crime," said Zafar Saidov, Rakhmonov's spokesman.

But at 5.30 p.m. (1230 GMT), Khudoyberdyev's forces had actually moved a checkpoint forward about 3 km (2 miles) towards Tursunzade from the town of Shakhrinau, about 12 km (7.5 miles) to the east of the aluminium town.
"We fought early this morning," Khudoyberdyev told reporters at Shakhrinau, where about 10 armoured vehicles and 200 of his men were stationed earlier in the day.

They prevented reporters from travelling on to Tursunzade but one of Khudoyberdyev's lieutenants said the rest of the brigade was now on the outskirts of the town, located close to the border with Uzbekistan.
One of Abdulayev's men was killed in the fighting, he added.
Diplomats say the war has caused armed bands -- fighting for control of the trade in Tajikistan's cotton, metals and narcotics -- to flourish.
Tursunzade, site of an aluminium smelter which produced 237,000 tonnes of the metal in 1995, has been the scene of clashes between rival armed gangs over the last 12 months.
Khudoyberdyev said his brigade had not targeted the plant but there was no word on whether production had been affected or who controlled the smelter.
